title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity
layout_note: A compact four-box Transformer block on the left is blown up by two dashed zoom lines into a large right panel that runs two tokens through the same block side by side.
grouping: Colour families by sublayer type: pink Add + Normalize, yellow Self-Attention, light-blue switching layer, green Router. In the enlarged panel the switching layer is a large rounded container with a thick blue border and a pale-blue fill holding both tokens' expert rows; residual paths are drawn as rectangular loops with rounded corners that wrap each sublayer.
shapes_depth: Flat rounded rectangles with thin outlines in a darker shade of their fill; no shadows. Each token is a row of six empty square cells (x1, x2 at the bottom with the words 'More' and 'Parameters' under them; y1, y2 at the top). Each expert is a small pale-blue rounded box (FFN 1-4); the router output is a tiny blue bar chart; multiply and add are circled-operator glyphs; the gate value travels as a dashed curved arrow labelled p = 0.65 / p = 0.8.
proposed_highlight: The proposed layer is light blue in both the compact stack ('Switching FFN Layer') and the zoomed container; inside it, the expert each token is routed to gets a bold black outline and bold text (FFN 2 for one token, FFN 1 for the other) while the unchosen experts stay thin.
lesson: Show sparse routing with two example tokens processed side by side through the same layer, each picking a different expert (bold outline) from an identical expert row, with a tiny bar chart of router probabilities under the row, so sparsity is seen rather than stated.
notes: 'other' element = the dashed zoom lines from the compact block to the enlarged panel. Venue and year from the PDF's first page (Journal of Machine Learning Research 23 (2022)).

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: in the expanded view two tokens, x1 'More' and x2 'Parameters', rise side by side through shared attention into one switching layer where each token's router picks a different expert (FFN 2 vs FFN 1, outlined bold)

relations.form: a compact four-block layer stack at the left is tied by two dashed lines to a large expanded view at the right that uses the same block colours
two token columns at equal spacing, each from an input cell row at the bottom to an output cell row y1 / y2 at the top
Self-Attention and both Add + Normalize boxes span both token columns, while the switching layer gives each token its own router and its own row of four expert boxes
each token sees the same row of four expert boxes FFN 1..FFN 4, the chosen one drawn with a bold black outline and bold label
a dashed curve carries the router's gate value (p = 0.65, p = 0.8) from the router up to a multiply node where it meets the chosen expert's output

channels.colour: layer type, the same in the compact stack and the expanded view: yellow = self-attention, red = add & normalize, light blue = the switching FFN layer and its experts, green = router; router probabilities are blue bar histograms
channels.shape: rows of empty cells = token vectors; small bar histograms = router distributions; circle-times = gating multiply, circle-plus = positional embedding add
channels.line: solid arrows = data; dashed curves = the gate value routed to the multiply; long outer lines = residual connections; a bold outline = the selected expert
channels.frame: a large rounded light-blue frame = the switching FFN layer

quality.strengths: The defining idea (per-token routing to one expert) is drawn as geometry: two tokens side by side select different experts from identical expert rows, with the router's distribution drawn as a histogram and the gate value attached; the compact stack teaches the layer once and the zoom spends the space on the new switching layer; colours keep one meaning across both views.
quality.weaknesses: The residual connections run as long outer loops around the full width of the panel; the dashed gate curves bend round the expert row to reach the multiply node; the gate value p floats beside its curve rather than at the multiply it scales.

insights.structure: A compact block stack on the left (Self-Attention, Add+Normalize, Switching FFN Layer, Add+Normalize) zooms via two dashed lines into a large expanded view on the right showing the same layer applied to two tokens side by side.
insights.data: Tokens are rows of empty cells labelled x1 'More' and x2 'Parameters'; router outputs are small blue bar histograms with the chosen probability (p = 0.65, p = 0.8) written beside them.
insights.emphasis: The switching FFN is a large light-blue rounded panel with a thick blue border; the selected expert (FFN 2 / FFN 1) is bold with a dark outline among four pale expert boxes.
insights.flow: Bottom to top: tokens + positional embedding -> shared attention -> per-token router -> one chosen expert -> multiply by gate -> Add+Normalize -> y1, y2; residual skips wrap round the outside as black loops.
insights.avoid: The dashed gate arrow from router to the multiply node loops widely around the experts and nearly collides with the 'p =' labels.

arrangement.units: a small overview stack at left and an enlarged detail at right linked by zoom lines; the routing layer is the one framed rounded panel
arrangement.inputs_as: token rows with the actual words written beneath
arrangement.shared: attention and Add+Normalize bars span both token columns; experts are per-token copies
